title: Access review
purpose: Read one signed access review: the accounts it covered, every grant with the decision to keep or remove it, whether each removal is done, the findings and follow-up, and the sign-off with its checksum. For holders of the review capability only.
summary: One signed access review: every grant reviewed with its decision, whether each grant decided for removal is still held, the findings and follow-up, and who signed it and when.

tasks.title: Check whether the removals are done
steps: Read [[To remove]]. [[Still held]] means the account still holds the grant now; [[No longer held]] means it does not.
For one still held, ask a superuser to remove it on the account's page in the admin console.

tasks.title: Check what was decided
steps: Read [[Every grant reviewed]] for each account's grants with Keep or Remove, and [[Findings]] and [[Follow-up]] for why.

tasks.title: Check the sign-off
steps: Read [[Sign-off]]. Under [[SHA-256 checksum]], Matches the access review as stored means it is as it was signed.

tasks.title: Keep the decisions
steps: Select [[Export CSV]]. The file holds one row for each grant, with whether each one decided for removal is held now.

good_to_know: Still held and No longer held are read as the accounts stand when the page opens. They are not part of what was signed.
A deactivated account holds nothing, so all its grants decided for removal show No longer held.
The access review cannot be changed or removed, and notes cannot be added to it.
A [[Checksum does not match]] notice means the stored access review differs from what was signed. Compare it with an earlier export or a backup.

items.label: Signed
items.description: Every access review is signed: there are no drafts.

items.label: Accounts reviewed
items.description: Shown beside Signed: Staff accounts, Client portal accounts, or Client portal accounts of one organization.

items.label: Removals still held
items.description: Shown when at least one grant decided for removal is still held now.

items.label: Export CSV
items.description: A spreadsheet file of the access review's decisions, one row for each grant in the order listed: Access review, Person, Username, Client organization, Grant, Detail, Decision, Held now (Yes or No for a grant decided for removal, read as the file is made; empty for a grant kept) and Signed at (with its offset). A cell that a spreadsheet would read as a formula starts with an apostrophe.

items.label: Accounts reviewed
items.description: Which accounts the access review covered: Staff accounts, Client portal accounts, or Client portal accounts of the organization named.

items.label: Accounts
items.description: How many accounts it listed: those in the choice that held something to review at signing.

items.label: Grants
items.description: How many grants it listed, each with a decision.

items.label: Decided to remove
items.description: How many grants the reviewer decided to remove.

items.label: Findings
items.description: What the reviewer found, as they wrote it. None recorded when empty.

items.label: Follow-up
items.description: Who removes what and by when, as the reviewer wrote it. None recorded when empty.

items.label: A grant decided for removal
items.description: The grant's words and detail, with the account's name, username and, for a portal account, its organization, as they were read for the signing. The count beside the heading is how many there are. Every grant was kept when there are none.

items.label: Still held
items.description: The account holds the grant now: it is active and still has the admin console access or superuser status, the membership of that role or group, or the capability given directly while its last day has not passed. A portal account is held while it is active in the organization it was reviewed in, whatever sites it may see now.

items.label: No longer held
items.description: The account does not hold the grant now, or it is deactivated or no longer exists. A deactivated account holds nothing. A capability given directly whose last day has passed by the database's clock is no longer held, though it stays on the account until it is removed.

items.label: How a grant is removed
items.description: Nothing on this page changes an account. A superuser removes roles, capabilities and admin console access, and deactivates a portal account, on the account's page in the admin console. Each such change is recorded in the change history.

items.label: An account
items.description: Its name and username, and for a portal account its organization, as they were read for the signing, in the order the form listed them.

items.label: A grant
items.description: Its words as the form showed them: Admin console, Superuser, a role such as Technical staff role, a group such as Group “night shift”, a capability with Given directly, or Portal account with what of its organization it could see; and Gives with the capability when a role or group gave one.

items.label: Keep or Remove
items.description: The reviewer's decision for the grant.

items.label: Signed by
items.description: The reviewer's name and username as they stood at signing. A later change to the account does not change them.

items.label: Roles held then
items.description: The reviewer's roles at signing, such as Supervisor. An account with the admin role shows Administrator alone.

items.label: Meaning
items.description: What the signature means: Reviewed, by the person who carried out the access review. It is the only meaning an access review is signed with.

items.label: Signed
items.description: The date and time of the signing, to the second, by the application's clock, in the laboratory's time zone. The grants were read just before it.

items.label: SHA-256 checksum
items.description: Taken at signing of exactly what was signed: the number, the accounts covered, every grant with its decision, the counts, the findings, the follow-up, the signer (account, name, username and roles), the meaning and the time. Each time the page opens it is taken again of the access review as stored and compared: Matches the access review as stored, or Does not match the access review as stored with a Checksum does not match notice above. Still held and No longer held are not covered. The checksum shows that the stored access review changed after signing; it does not say who changed it. The application never changes an access review, and the database refuses to.

items.label: How it was signed
items.description: Record an access review asks for the reviewer's password at each signing, and not the second factor. A demonstration's example access review is written by its seed without one.

sections.title: Who can use this page
paragraphs: Staff with a laboratory role who hold the capability Can review access and audit records. Everyone else is refused. A number that names no access review shows Not found.

Each time the page is shown and each export is recorded under Workspace use in Audit review, with the source Access review: reviews and the access review's number. If the record cannot be written, nothing is shown or exported.
